rows.why: The stem never says what is plotted: the axes log([R]0/[R]) against t and the line's passage through the origin are read off the graph, and parts (a) order and (b) slope are exactly those readings.
Same question on another set: order and slope are readings of a graph whose axes the stem never names, so neither (a) nor (b) can be answered from the text.
Whether the substance is diamagnetic (Copper) or ferro/paramagnetic turns entirely on whether the field lines are expelled from or crowded into the block, and the stem states neither.
'Four half reactions I to IV are shown below' triggered the rule, but all four half-equations are written out in the stem itself - nothing is printed elsewhere.
The only relation needed, AC = (5/4) AB, is given in the stem; the figure adds nothing beyond A, B, C being collinear.
Set member (shared context): the context gives the cone-plus-cylinder shape, the 45-degree semi-vertical angle and the 2 cm^3/s drain rate, which is everything V = (1/3)pi r^3 needs.
Set member: r = 2*sqrt(2) cm and dV/dt = -2 cm^3/s are both in the stem and context; the tank drawing supplies no number.
Set member: the wet-surface rate follows from h = r (from the stated 45-degree semi-vertical angle) and the given radius, none of it read off the figure.
Set member: slant height 4 cm is given in the stem and h = r comes from the stated semi-vertical angle, so the figure is decorative.
Set member: the context states the wall runs along one side, wire fences the other three, and 200 m of wire is available - the whole model 2x + y = 200.
Set member: maximising A(x) = 200x - 2x^2 uses only the relation established in part (i), not the garden sketch.

The context's 'The following graph shows the sine function' names the standard sine curve, not a printed diagram this part uses; the question asks only for principal values of sin^-1(-1/2) and sin^-1(1).
'Draw the graph of \(\sin^{-1} x\) from \([-1, 1]\) to its principal value branch.' - the student produces the figure.
Domain and range of 2 sin^-1(1-x) is pure algebra on the arcsine's domain; the context's mention of the sine graph names a known curve, not a needed picture.

Set member of the photoelectric case study: the context already states the V0-nu plot is 'a straight line of slope m', and this part asks only how wave number and frequency scale when the wavelength doubles - note siblings (i)-(iii)(a) of the same set DO carry the image, so the attach is partial.
Set member: lambda = h/p needs only the momentum given in this row; nothing in the V0-nu graph enters, though the same set's earlier parts carry the image and these two do not.
The waveform of the inductor current over the cycle exists only in the graph, and V = L dI/dt makes the answer a reading of that graph's slope - the stem gives no shape for I.
'The given circuit' is where the 24-ohm resistor, the series ideal ammeter and the parallel ideal voltmeter live; the stem names not one resistance, so no pair of readings can be tested.
Clockwise versus anticlockwise depends on the sense in which the coil is wound on the arm and on the orientation of the U-magnet's poles, both visible only in the figure.
'The given circuit' supplies the three branches (5 V with 2 ohm, 10 V with 1 ohm, plain 2 ohm) and the opposing cell polarities; the stem states no emf, resistance or polarity.
Set member: 'shown below in the table' triggered the rule and the table of five javelin distances is printed inline in the context, along with the 40% and 90% figures this part uses.
Set member: total probability over the stated 40/60 split with the given 80% and 10% conditionals - all in the context's prose and inline table.
Set member: Bayes' theorem on the percentages given in the context; nothing is read from a picture.
Set member: the complementary Bayes computation on the same inline data.

'Deduce the expressions for the force acting on length L of conductor B due to conductor A and show it in figure' - the student draws the force directions; the currents, the separation d and the length L are all given.
Set member: the ellipse 9x^2 + 16y^2 = 144 is given in the context, so making y the subject needs nothing from the track drawing.
Set member: integrating the function from part (i) is pure calculus on a stated equation.
Set member: the region excluding the track is the ellipse whose equation the context gives, and the 3 m track width is stated too.
Set member: the vertices A(0,4), B(-2,0), C(3,0) are listed in the context, which is all the equation of AB needs.
Set member: AC joins the two stated intercept points (0,4) and (3,0); the park sketch adds nothing.
Set member: region OAC is fixed by the stated vertices and the line AC found in part (ii).
Set member: region AOB is bounded by the y-axis, the stated B(-2,0) and the line AB from part (i).
Set member: the context states the cup is conical, 15 cm deep, radius 5 cm, filled at 0.1 cm^3/s, so r = h tan(alpha) follows from the words alone.
Set member: dh/dt at h = 6 cm uses only the stated cup dimensions and pour rate.
Set member: the surface area pi r^2 with r = h/3 comes from the stated 15 cm depth and 5 cm radius.
Set member: the wetted-surface rate uses the same stated cup geometry, not the party sketch.
'shown in the following table' triggered the rule; the four-box colour table is printed inline in the stem, so the Bayes computation is fully supported.
Set member: the shared context is only 'In Fig 10.5, which of the vectors are:' and this row's entire text is the fragment 'Collinear' - the vectors a, b, c, d exist only in Fig 10.5.
Set member: the text is the bare fragment 'Equal'; which vectors share magnitude and direction is a property of the drawing alone.
Set member: the text is the bare fragment 'Coinitial'; the common initial point is visible only in Fig 10.5.

The circuit is described in words - a light bulb and an open-coil inductor in series with an ac source through a key - and the answer turns on the inserted iron rod raising L, not on reading Fig. 7.9.
The cube of twelve 1-ohm resistors with a 10 V battery across a body diagonal is fully specified in the stem; the symmetry argument needs no printed drawing.
'Determine the current in each branch of the network shown in Fig. 3.17' - the stem names no emf, no resistance and no topology at all.
All four bridge arms (100, 10, 5, 60 ohm), the 15-ohm galvanometer across BD and the 10 V across AC are stated, so the mesh equations can be written from the text.
The cube's placement is only in Fig. 1.24: the solution needs x = a at the left face and x = 2a at the right, plus which two faces are shaded, and the stem gives only alpha and a.
The cylinder's length, radius and the positions of its two faces at x = +/-10 cm are all stated, as are the two field values.
Each stage of Fig. 1.4(a)-(c) is narrated in the stem, including the 10 cm and 5.0 cm centre separations and the touching by identical uncharged spheres C and D.
Three charges q at the vertices of an equilateral triangle of side l with Q at the centroid is stated in full; the figure only labels them.

The stem gives neither the triangle's side length (the solution's l) nor which vertex carries the -q, and every direction in the answer is quoted relative to the vertices A, B, C that only Fig. 1.7 labels.
The 1.5 cm fall, the 2.0x10^4 N/C field and the reversal of its direction for the proton are all in the stem; Fig. 1.10(a)/(b) only label the two cases.
Where A, B and C sit is only in Fig. 1.11 - the solution uses 0.05 m and 0.15 m separations that the stem never states.
P is stated to be 15 cm from O on the axis on the positive-charge side and Q 15 cm from O on the normal, so both dipole fields follow from the text.
The loops' shapes and each one's direction of motion into or out of the field region are entirely in Fig. 6.7; the stem enumerates none of them.
Part (d), 'Predict the polarity of the capacitor in the situation described by Fig. 6.9', describes nothing in words, and part (c) leans on the loop arrangement drawn in Fig. 6.8.
The 1 m rod, 50 rev/s rotation, 1 m ring radius and 1 T axial field are all stated; emf = B*omega*L^2/2 follows from the text.
Both capacitances (900 pF each) and the 100 V charging supply are stated, and Fig. 2.31(a)/(b) only label the before and after connections.

The stem carries a written-out '[Read from Fig. 2.8: ...]' account of both field-line patterns and of P/Q and A/B lying on the same side with the nearer point named - answerable as printed (note the marker is not the '[Figure:' form describesFigureInText looks for).
'[Read from Fig. 2.15: ...]' names the charge at each corner of square ABCD and identifies E as the centre, so both work computations are supported; again the marker is not '[Figure:'.
'[Fig. 2.29 shows the network as follows ...]' spells out the C1-C2-C3 series chain from A to D with C4 in parallel across it.
Mass 200 g, length 1.5 m and current 2 A are stated and mid-air suspension fixes mg = IlB; Fig. 4.3 only illustrates.
The stem restates the circuit in words - a 3.00 V source in series with a 3.00-ohm resistor and the ammeter - so all three cases are computable.
B along +y and v along +x are stated, which is all the v x B direction needs; Fig. 4.4 only draws the axes.
The current element at the origin, I = 10 A, Delta x = 1 cm and the 0.5 m point on the y-axis are all given.
The 12 A current and the 2.0 cm semicircular arc are stated, and part (c)'s alternative is described in words as the arc 'bent in the opposite way'.
A long straight wire of radius a carrying a uniformly distributed steady current I is stated in the stem - that is the whole Ampere's-law derivation for r < a and r > a.
Covering the lower half of a concave mirror's reflecting surface is fully stated; the answer (whole image, reduced intensity) needs no reading of Fig. 9.6.
'Show by suitable diagram, the formation of its image' - the student draws the ray diagram, and the phone lying along the principal axis is stated in words.
'[Fig. 9.20 shows ...]' supplies the three focal lengths (+10, -10, +30 cm), the 30 cm object distance and the 5 cm and 10 cm lens separations.

The 1 mm^2 size of each square is not in this row - it lives in Exercise 9.23's figure - so |m| = sqrt(6.25/1) = 2.5 cannot be formed from this stem; the repair is a cross-reference to 9.23 as much as an image.
The resistances are readings of the V-I characteristic - V at I = 10 mA and 20 mA for the forward slope, and the reverse leakage current at -10 V - and the stem gives no point on the curve.
